paragraphs.text: Heb., Of the book. It is taken for any manner of writing, whether longer, as a book, or shorter, as a letter, an epistle, cuius ornamentum est ornamentis carere, saith Politian; the two chief commendations whereof, say others, are shortness and plainness. Here we have both, and should therefore highly prize it, not as apocryphal Baruch’s letter, but as parcel of holy writ, worthy of all acceptation.
paragraphs.anchor: Now these are the words of the letter.

paragraphs.text: And longed for deliverance; but are advised to have patience, and not to antedate the promises, which in their due time should be accomplished. As till then obediendum est etiam dyscolis, obedience must be yielded to the Babylonians, now their masters, and "not only to the good and gentle, but also to the froward; for this is thankworthy." {1Pe 2:18}
paragraphs.anchor: Which were carried away captive.

paragraphs.text: Angusta et eunuchi. These eunuchs were chamberlains to queens; but not always so bold with them as Stephen the Persian presumed to be with the queen mother of the emperor Justinian II: quam flagellis sicuti servam castigavit whom he corrceted with a whip just as a servant. {a} See Jer 24:1-2.
paragraphs.anchor: After that Jeconiah the king, and the queen, and the eunuchs.

paragraphs.text: {a} Func.

Zedekiah, having heard by Hananiah the prophet, that within two full years Jeconiah and the captives should come back to Jerusalem, and knowing that if that should be so, he must give place and part with his royal dignity, sendeth an embassy to Nebuchadnezzar to show his obsequiousness, and is content that his messenger should carry Jeremiah’s letters (of whom, haply, he had a better conceit after the death of Hananiah) to those of the captivity, to persuade them to live quietly in Babylon, and not yet to think of returning to his disturbance. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: By the hand of Elasah the son of Shaphan, &c.

paragraphs.text: {a} Calvin.

It was God, then, that dictated this letter to the prophet; neither is it of private, that is, of human interpretation, but the holy man wrote it as he was moved thereunto by the Holy Ghost. {2Pe 1:20-21}
paragraphs.anchor: Thus saith the Lord of hosts.

paragraphs.text: Mitigate the extremity of your captivity, which is likely to be long, by all honest means. Levius fit patientia quicquid corrigere est nefas; patience, as a paring knife, cutteth the cross less and less till it comes to nothing. It teacheth a man, in case he cannot bring his estate to his mind, to bring his mind to his estate, and that is as well; but impatiens quisque bis affligitur; the bullock under the yoke gets nothing by wriggling but galling.
paragraphs.anchor: Build ye houses, and dwell in them.

paragraphs.text: First get ye houses and gardens, and then take wives. So in the last commandment house is set before wife; and nature teacheth the birds to build their nests before they come together for copulation.
paragraphs.anchor: Take ye wives, and beget sons.

paragraphs.text: Do not tumultuate or seek to break prison, as those seedsmen of sedition, your false prophets, would persuade you, but frame to a peaceable and patient behaviour. "In returning and rest shall ye be saved, in quietness and in confidence shall be your strength" {Isa 30:15}
paragraphs.anchor: And seek the peace of the city.

paragraphs.text: sc., That in it you may "lead a peaceable and quiet life, in all godliness and honesty." {1Ti 2:2} Christians should improve their waiting months upon the King of saints, to pray for kings and all that are in authority, though to them they had been tyrants, since it seemeth good to God that they should live under them. The Dutch have a proverb,
paragraphs.anchor: And pray unto God for it

paragraphs.text: “ Arbor honoretur, cuius nos umbra tuetur. ”

Your deceivers, indeed, which were also in Babylon as well as at Jerusalem; for all places are full of them, aud so is hell too. But "beware of these dogs, beware of evil workers"; {Php 3:2} three of them, the most active, no doubt, are here noted and noticed {Jer 29:21; Jer 29:23} with a charge in this text, Ne committitote ut decipiant vos; see that they deceive you not. The body should be kept, say physicians, in habitu athletico, in a vigorous and healthy temper, able to oppose infections. Think the same of the soul.
paragraphs.anchor: Let not your prophets and your diviners.

paragraphs.text: "Yours," because you itch after them, listen to them, pay dearly for them.
paragraphs.anchor: Neither hearken to your dreams.

paragraphs.text: As Jer 27:15; Jer 28:15.
paragraphs.anchor: For they prophesy falsely.

paragraphs.text: Or, But this hath the Lord said, whatever these impostors say to the contrary. Set truth against falsehood, and it will silence it, like as if a lamp be hanged over a ditch where frogs are croaking, they are forthwith hushed and made quiet.
paragraphs.anchor: For thus saith the Lord.

paragraphs.text: God’s thoughts run upon his children, the children of affliction especially, as a father’s do upon his dear children. Omnis in Ascanio, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: For I know the thoughts that I think.

paragraphs.text: Heb., An end and expectation - i.e., An end of evils past, and expectation of better for the future.
paragraphs.anchor: To give you an expected end.

paragraphs.text: With mind and mouth, with spirit and speech, as Daniel did, {Dan 9:3} and as but few others did, during the captivity, as is confessed. {Dan 9:13}
paragraphs.anchor: Then shall ye call upon me.

paragraphs.text: Go into your closets, or other oratories, where you shall pour out your hearts unto me.
paragraphs.anchor: And go and pray unto me.

paragraphs.text: Which shall be a surer seal of my love than your return from Babylon.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will hearken unto you.

paragraphs.text: Not with a piece of your heart only, as do partialists and double minded men, qui in parabola ovis capras quaerunt. who search for a nanny goat instaed of sheep. Johannes Groppcrus, of Colen, refused a cardinalship, but forsook the gospel. So Luther did not, who, when he was offered to be cardinal if he would be quiet, replied, No, not if I might be Pope. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: When ye shall search for me with all your heart.

paragraphs.text: {a} Sleidan.
The best ευρημα. See Psa 32:6 Isa 55:6; Isa 65:1.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will be found of you.

paragraphs.text: As my scattered jewels. See Jer 13:7; Jer 24:6.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will gather you.

paragraphs.text: From the heirs of the promises he turneth his speech to others, qui praesumendo sperant, et sperando pereunt.
paragraphs.anchor: Because ye have said.

paragraphs.text: Or, Therefore thus saith the Lord, whatever ye say, or your counterfeit prophets say, to the contrary.
paragraphs.anchor: Know that thus saith the Lord.
Behold, I will send upon them.

paragraphs.text: See Jer 24:8.
paragraphs.anchor: And will make them like vile figs.

paragraphs.text: See Jer 15:4; Jer 24:9.
paragraphs.anchor: And will deliver them to be removed.
Because they have not hearkened.

paragraphs.text: Or, Hear ye also; ye who have lost the fruit of your afflictions, and are little the better for your being so long in the iron furnace.
paragraphs.anchor: Hear ye, therefore.

paragraphs.text: Thus saith the Lord … of Ahab the son of Kolaiah.] These two - though not the two elders that assaulted Susanna, as some have fabled - are singled out, as arch-imposters and filthy adulterers, to be exemplarily punished; to whom also is added Shemaiah the Nehelamite. {Jer 29:24}

Vide autem iustam poenam martyrum diaboli, saith Oecolampadius. See here the just punishment of the devil’s martyrs: this evil couple had prophesied, like, the destruction of Babylon, bade the Jews put themselves in a posture to return home, promised to conduct them to Jerusalem, played many lewd pranks besides, and were therefore worthily put to a cruel death by Nebuchadnezzar, in the presence of their friends and followers.
paragraphs.anchor: And he shall slay them before your eyes.

paragraphs.text: They had blessed themselves, though the Lord abhorred them, and sought to set up themselves in the hearts of the people, being gloriae animalia, popularis aurae vilissima mancipia, as Jerome saith of Crates the philosopher; they shall therefore "leave their names for a curse." {as Isa 65:15}
paragraphs.anchor: And of them shall be taken up a curse.

paragraphs.text: Burnt them with a soft slow fire, as the Papists did John Huss, Bishop Ridley, and many other innocent martyrs; but should do rather these filthy Gergesites, their monks and friars, of whom it went for a proverb in Germany, as Luther witnesseth, Whosoever seeth any one of them, seeth the seven deadly sins.
paragraphs.anchor: Whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire.

paragraphs.text: Because they have committed adultery with their neighbours’ wives.] As did Eli’s sons, {1Sa 2:22} those false prophets also at Jerusalem, {Jer 23:14} Hetser, the great Anabaptist in Germany, {a} who yet died penitently, and as do still the Imailers, an order of religious men among the Turks, {b} who call them the religious brothers of love, and the Brahmins, successors to the Brachmanni, among the Indians, who are extremely impure and libidinous, claiming the first night’s lodging of every bride, &c., having nothing of a man but the voice and shape, and yet these are their priests. {c}

Let them carry their villany never so cleanly and closely, with their si non caste, saltem caute, yet I know all, am now an eyewitness, and will be one day a swift witness against them. Utinam animadverterent haec principes, et ille qui non in sede Petri sed in prostibulo Priapi Lampsaceni sedens fornieationes tegit, sancta coniuga vetat, mera sorenia vendit, et Dei oculos claudit, saith one.
paragraphs.anchor: Even I know, and am a witness, saith the Lord.

paragraphs.text: {a} Scultet. Annal.
{b} Turk. Hist., 477.
{c} Heyl., Cosmog.
Or, Dreamer, dream wright, enthusiast; such as were the Messalanian heretics of old, and some of the same stamp, loaves of the same leaven, today.
paragraphs.anchor: Thus shalt thou also speak to Shemaiah the Nehelamite.

paragraphs.text: Such as Sadoletus, a Popish bishop, sent to Geneva in Calvin’s absence, to bring them back again to the obedience of the see of Rome; and as we have many from the Romish factors sent hither, to the seducing of not a few, a subtle and shrewd way of deceiving the simple.
paragraphs.anchor: Because thou hast sent letters in thy name.

paragraphs.text: The second under the high priest Seraiah, and successor likely to that Pashur {Jer 20:1} who was deposed for some misdemeanour, like as Dr Weston was here in Queen Mary’s days, put by all his Church dignities for being taken in bed with a harlot. {a} Of this Zephaniah, see 2Ki 25:18, his office was to judge of prophecies, and to punish such as he found to be false prophets.
paragraphs.anchor: And to Zephaniah.

paragraphs.text: Who were much too forward of themselves to bandy against God’s true prophets, {Jer 26:8} and did as little need by letter to be excited thereunto, as Bishop Bonner did to be stirred up to persecute Protestants; and yet to him were letters sent from King Philip and Queen Mary, complaining that heretics were not so reformed as they should be, and exhorting him to more diligence, {b} &c.
paragraphs.anchor: And to all the priests.

paragraphs.text: {a} Acts and Mon.
{b} Clarke’s Martyrol., 136.

That heroic reformer in the days of Joash {2Ki 11:4; 2Ki 11:17} Therefore, as he did by Mattan the Baalite, so do thou by Jeremiah the Anathothite. But neither was Zephaniah a Jehoiada, nor Jeremiah a Mattan. Shemaiah himself was more like a Baalite, and better deserved that punishment which shortly after also befell him, as was foretold. {Jer 29:32} A hot spirited man he was, and a firebrand, being therefore the more dangerous. He also seemed to himself to be so much the more holy, by how much the prophet whom he set against was more famous for his holiness.
paragraphs.anchor: The Lord hath made thee priest instead of Jehoiada the priest.

paragraphs.text: Maniacus, arreptitius, fanaticus; so God’s zealous servants have always been esteemed by the mad world, ever beside itself in point of salvation. See 2Ki 9:11 Act 26:24 Jer 43:2.
paragraphs.anchor: For every one that is mad.

paragraphs.text: As Jer 20:2.
paragraphs.anchor: That thou shouldest put him in prison.

paragraphs.text: Or, Restrained Jeremiah? Alas! what had the righteous prophet done? He taxed their sin, he foretold their captivity; he desired it not, he inflicted it not, yet he must smart, and they are guilty. Zephaniah also is here blamed for his lenity, as bloody Bonner once was by the rest of the Popish bishops, who made him their slaughter slave.
paragraphs.anchor: Now, therefore, why hast thou not reproved?

paragraphs.text: And is this all the thank he hath for his friendly counsel? Haec est merces mundi. This is the recompence of the world.
paragraphs.anchor: For therefore he sent to us in Babylon.

paragraphs.text: For ill will, likely, and with exprobation. Ubi insignis elucit Dei tutela, saith an interpreter, where we may see a sweet providence of God in preserving his prophet from the rage and violence of the people so incensed.
paragraphs.anchor: And Zephaniah the priest read this letter.

paragraphs.text: Or, Therefore came, &c. In the five former verses we had narrationem causae, an account of the reasons Shemaiah’s crime; in these three last, we have dictionem sententiae, the prediction of the sentence Shemaiah’s doom.
paragraphs.anchor: Then came the word of the Lord.

paragraphs.text: Send the second time; let not so good a cause be deserted. Vincet aliquando pertinax bonitas, Truth will take place at length.
paragraphs.anchor: Send to all them of the captivity.

paragraphs.text: He hath rewarded evil thereby to himself, and to his seed after him; his posterity shall rue for it, saith Jeremiah, who was irrefracti plane animi orator, a man of an invincible courage, and might better have been called Doctor resolutus, than was afterwards Bacon the Carmelite.
paragraphs.anchor: Because Shemaiah hath prophesied unto you.

paragraphs.text: As being part of his goods, and walking likely in his evil ways.
paragraphs.anchor: Behold, I will punish Shemaiah, and his seed.

paragraphs.text: viz., At the return from Babylon; but both he and his shall perish in this banishment, which he prophesied should be shortly at an end, but shall prove it otherwise. See the like, Amo 7:17.
paragraphs.anchor: He shall not have a man to dwell among this people

paragraphs.text: He nor any of his. See the like threatened to that unbelieving prince, 2Ki 7:2.
paragraphs.anchor: Neither shall he see the good.

paragraphs.text: So Jer 28:16 Jer 23:27 Mat 5:19. To be tuba rebellionis trumpet of rebellion is no small fault. Luther was so secundum dici, sed non secundum esse; so may the best be; but let not the sins of teachers be teachers of sins, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: Because he hath taught rebellion against the Lord.
